title: Pair the Gloves
statement: A lost-and-found box holds single gloves, each labeled with a size number. Two gloves make a pair when they have the same size, and each glove can be in at most one pair. Return the largest number of pairs you can make.

answerKey.pattern: Sort so equal sizes sit together, then walk and pair neighbors (or count each size and add count / 2)
keyPoints: After sorting, gloves of the same size are next to each other
Walk from the left: if a glove and the next one match, count a pair and skip both
Otherwise move on by one glove
A hash map of counts with count / 2 per size is also correct
answerKey.timeComplexity: O(n log n) with sorting, O(n) with a count map
answerKey.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra after an in-place sort, or O(k) for k sizes
edgeCases: An odd number of gloves of one size
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Searching for a partner for each glove: O(n²)

hints: Which gloves can pair up? Where would they be if the sizes were in order?
Sort the sizes. Now any matching gloves are neighbors.
Walk with an index i: if sizes[i] equals sizes[i + 1], count a pair and jump by 2; otherwise step by 1.
